what_was_done.action: Handle HTTP 412 from the action route as a refusal, not an HTTP failure (architecture § Seam 5 defense-in-depth)
what_was_done.result: Modified the existing `if (!res.ok) throw` path at the rule's fetch site. New branch ahead of the throw: if res.status === 412, read body, log warn-line tagged `reconciler_dispatch_refused_at_route` with httpStatus + body, appendEvent of type RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED with refusalCode='ROUTE_REFUSED_412' + failedCheck='route-side-precondition' + reason=<body>, return without throwing. Distinguishes route-side precondition refusal (race window between rule check and route check) from a genuine HTTP failure that the existing throw path handles.

deviations_from_ac: None material. Two clarifications: (1) The bead description text uses two slightly different identifiers — 'reconciler_dispatch_refused' and 'reconciler_dispatch_refused_at_route' — for the structured warn-log line, while the EVENT-LOG entry type is the existing 'reconciler-action-refused' (Wave-1 constant from ehp.2). The implementation honours both: warn-line tags use the underscore-form per the bead text (greppable as `[xfc] reconciler_dispatch_refused`); event-log entries use the canonical hyphen-form RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED constant. Route-side refusals are distinguished in the event payload via refusalCode='ROUTE_REFUSED_412' + failedCheck='route-side-precondition'. (2) The OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING test fixture uses stage='coherence' so interpretMarkerForRouting's Precedence 1.5 escape hatch preserves the operator routing through to send-for-review, exercising the OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING precondition against the genuine downstream action. With stage='builder' (loop-agent) the marker would be rewritten to coherence by interpretMarkerForRouting — the precondition would still fire (it inspects the raw marker), but the test would be testing the rewrite path rather than the operator-decision path. The chosen fixture is the cleaner read.
surprises_or_findings:
1. The reconciler core (reconciler.ts:381) appends `reconciler-action-taken` UNCONDITIONALLY after every act() returns (whether refused or successful) — this consumes the (rule, key) idempotency bucket even on refusals. Architecture ADR-006 calls for refusals to live in a SEPARATE bucket keyed (epicId, ruleName, refusalCode, 15-min window). Implementing the separate bucket requires a reconciler.ts change which is OUT OF SCOPE for ehp.4 per the bead's risk-flag guidance ('defer to reconciler.ts's existing window helper or document the gap as FOLLOW-ON'). Documented as FOLLOW-ON in this marker's recommendation_for_next AND inline in marker-driven-routing.ts's precondition-gate comment.
2. interpretMarkerForRouting's Precedence 1.5 (factory-core-wlsr.3 ADR-001) rewrites next_agent='operator' to 'coherence' for loop-agent stages with stage!='coherence'. This means a marker with next_agent='operator' + stage='builder' (the most common operator-pending shape for loop agents) would route to coherence, NOT to operator. The OPERATOR_DECISION_PENDING precondition still fires correctly (it inspects the raw marker, not the rewritten next_agent) — verified by the integration test. The test uses stage='coherence' to exercise the cleaner case where operator routing is preserved through the rewrite layer.
3. Adding the precondition gate broke 4 pre-existing tests that didn't mock the readers (legacy synthetic-bead tests). The fix is a 30-line jest.mock block at file-top in each affected test — pattern lifted from __tests__/lib/dispatch-preconditions.test.ts. Surfaced and applied per the in-scope 'no regressions on existing tests' invariant; not a scope deviation since the fix is mock-only (no behaviour change in the legacy tests).
4. The orphan-recovery integration test (marker-driven-routing.orphan-recovery.test.ts:412) uses `await import('@/lib/marker-reader')` to fetch the real readMarker, but the new file-level jest.mock intercepts that. Fix: replace with `jest.requireActual('@/lib/marker-reader')` so the test still gets the real filesystem reader for its synthetic marker file. One-line fix.
whats_open: FOLLOW-ON (separate reconciler-core bead): refusals consume the `reconciler-action-taken` idempotency bucket because reconciler.ts:381 appends that event unconditionally after act() returns. Architecture ADR-006 calls for a SEPARATE bucket keyed (epicId, ruleName, refusalCode, 15-min window). Suggested approach: have act() return a tagged result {kind: 'taken' | 'refused', refusalCode?} and have the reconciler core branch on it (taken → existing append, refused → new bucket). This requires touching reconciler.ts's per-rule idempotency window helper. Not load-bearing for the 372-bead defer (the rule still refuses correctly every tick — refusing again 15 min later is the same refusal), but matters for the 'transient refusal crowds out a real dispatch' edge case the ADR calls out.

FOLLOW-ON: beads_web-ehp.13 (Wave-3 parallel sibling) extends dispatch-preconditions.ts with per-action predicates (Class A: 5; B: 3; D: 1; E: 1) and adds the PreconditionRefusalResponse helper.
